title: Evidence Reliability Receipt
description: Article-level W3C Verifiable Credential summarizing negative signals at publish time. Clean receipt = no flags. Any flags present = investigate via component pointers.

@context.description: W3C VC context URIs. Includes OriginVault receipt context.

id.description: DID URI of this receipt on the article's cheqd identity. Corrections produce new receipt IDs on the same article DID.

issuer.description: DID of issuing entity. Phase 1: OriginVault's signing DID. Phase 2+: org-specific signing DID.

credentialStatus.description: Bitstring status list entry on org's mainnet DID. This is the payment gate for downstream verification.

statusPurpose.description: Revocation = article retracted. Suspension = correction in progress.

statusListCredential.description: DID URL to status list resource on org's mainnet DID.

credentialSchema.description: Points to this schema for downstream validation.

article.description: Article identity. The DID is the persistent anchor that accumulates correction history.

did.description: Article DID on cheqd testnet. Persistent across corrections.

url.description: Canonical article URL at publish time.

supersedes.description: Receipt ID of the previous version if this is a correction. Null for first publish.

publisher.description: Organization identity. Resolved via contributor identity credentials, not the signing cert.

trust_framework.description: DID URL to the org's trust framework resource on cheqd. Tells a downstream consumer what standard this org commits to.

evaluation_summary.description: High-level triage data. A consumer reads this first. If overall_status is 'pass' and remaining_flags is empty, the article is clean - stop here.

profile_ref.description: Which Trust Profile was used. Pointer + hash so a downstream consumer can verify the standard without fetching it.

profile_id.description: DID URL or URI of the Trust Profile used.

profile_hash.description: Hash of the profile at evaluation time. Proves which version of the rules were applied.

evaluated_at.description: When evaluation was performed. May differ from publish time if evaluation was cached.

overall_status.description: 'pass' = zero remaining flags. 'flagged' = one or more flags survived to publish (acknowledged or unacknowledged). No 'fail' - publishing with flags is an editorial choice, not a system failure.

remaining_flags.description: NEGATIVE SIGNALS ONLY. Flags that survived to publish. Resolved flags do not appear - their absence is the positive signal. Empty array = clean article.

components.description: Pointers to per-component trust reports. Not the reports themselves - just enough to discover and resolve them. A consumer who wants depth follows these pointers.

remaining_flag.description: A single negative signal that survived to publish. Two types: acknowledged (editor made a judgment) and unacknowledged (gap exists, no one addressed it). The difference is the entire editorial trust signal.

indicator_id.description: Trust Project indicator this flag belongs to. e.g., 'journalist_expertise', 'methods', 'locally_sourced', 'references'. Lets a downstream consumer filter by the indicators they care about.

flag_type.description: Specific flag from the risk registry. e.g., 'missing_photographer_identity', 'no_capture_device_info', 'ai_generation_markers_present', 'unsigned_content'. Registry URI resolvable for remediation guidance.

flag_registry_ref.description: URI to the flag definition in the risk registry. Provides severity rationale, remediation guidance, and context a downstream consumer may need.

severity.description: From risk registry. Informs downstream triage priority.

disposition.description: The core editorial signal. 'acknowledged' = an editor reviewed this gap and accepted it. 'unacknowledged' = the gap exists and no one on the editorial team addressed it.

acknowledged_by.description: Editor/reporter identifier (WordPress user ID or contributor DID). Present only when disposition is 'acknowledged'. Null otherwise.

acknowledged_at.description: Timestamp of acknowledgment. Present only when disposition is 'acknowledged'. Null otherwise.

component_hash.description: If this flag is specific to one content block (e.g., a single image missing photographer identity), reference the component. Null if the flag is article-level or org-level.

component_ref.description: Pointer to a content block's embedded trust report. The trust report carries the full positive + negative signal detail. The receipt only carries the negatives.

content_hash.description: Hash of the content block. Anchored on the article DID for recovery when platforms strip provenance.

content_type.description: MIME type. Phase 1: image/*. Phase 2+: text, video, etc.

c2pa_manifest_present.description: Whether a C2PA manifest was present at evaluation time. Lets a downstream consumer know whether provenance chain existed for this component.

trust_report_ref.description: DID URL or content-addressed URI to the full trust report embedded in or associated with this component. Null if the component had no evaluable provenance.

verificationMethod.description: DID key URI of the signing key. Phase 1: OriginVault's key. Phase 2+: org's key.
